experiment: MSU-2 Task 2e paired sustained AXI Quad SPI comparison
date: 2026-10-16 local workstation date; JTAG evidence collected 2026-10-17 UTC

workload.integrity: every completed transfer compared byte-for-byte with deterministic transmitted pattern
workload.metric: verified payload bytes / measured application window; application payload rate, not wire throughput
workload.backend_order: all Linux windows preceded all bare-metal windows; backend order was not alternated

serial_sck_hz.physical_j55_measurement: approximately 51000000 Hz, measured 2026-09-29 for the same bitstream and ratio-2 setting; not simultaneous with sustained windows

a53_hz.sampling_scope: read-only JTAG snapshot after bare-metal run; not sampled during each point

software.linux_cpu_point: userspace governor, 1200000 kHz, captured before the sustained set; not sampled per point
software.baremetal: Vitis 2025.1 standalone A53; XSpi interrupt driver with busy-wait completion loop; XTime_GetTime
software.baremetal_cpu_metric: 100% dedicated-core busy-wait occupancy inferred from execution model; not a PMU measurement

results.crossover: bare metal faster at 1-16 bytes; Linux faster at 64 bytes and larger

limits: This is a maximum observed application rate under the defined 60-second windows, not a universal hardware ceiling or clock/payload stress envelope.
Physical J55 SCK was not remeasured during sustained windows.
CPU and clock rates were not sampled at each point; A53 register-derived rate is a post-run readback.
Backend order was not alternated; order and thermal effects are uncontrolled.
Different API/timer execution models prevent causal attribution of rate differences to Linux kernel overhead alone.
Bare-metal busy-wait occupancy must not be interpreted as a PMU CPU-utilization reading.

evidence.validation_result: 33 bare-metal points; 11 payload sizes; 3 repetitions; zero errors or mismatches
